title: Team session rendering and import improvements
description:
## Problem
Team sessions imported into Spotter have multiple rendering and UX deficiencies:
1. No auto-import of sister sessions with the same teamName — each team member must be imported individually
2. Timeline entries overlap in lanes view — no time-proportional positioning
3. Lane columns render raw message data instead of piping through TranscriptRenderer, resulting in missing tool blocks, code blocks, and markdown
4. Lane tab bar lacks drag-and-drop reorder capability
Additionally, teammate-message XML tags in message content are now classified correctly (Bug #4 fix landed) but still need styled rendering in the frontend.

## Solution
1. Add team-aware grouping to transcript discovery and "Import Team" bulk action
2. Render each lane through TranscriptRenderer pipeline for full-fidelity display
3. Fix timeline positioning or switch to independent scrollable panels per lane
4. Add SortableJS-based drag-and-drop to lane tab bar with persisted order

## Rabbit Holes
- Time-proportional timeline layout is complex and may not be the right UX — consider independent scrollable panels instead
- Auto-import could be slow if many team sessions exist — need pagination or lazy loading
- SortableJS dependency weight and LiveView hook integration complexity

## No-gos
- No authentication/authorization changes
- No schema migrations for lane order (use socket assigns only for now)
- No changes to the JSONL parser — team messages use standard types with embedded XML

---

title: Auto-import sister team sessions
description:
## Why this task is needed now
When importing a team session, users must manually select each team member's JSONL file individually. There is no way to import all team members at once, leading to partial imports and confusion about which sessions belong together.

## Output files
- lib/spotter/services/transcript_discovery.ex (add team_name to preview map, group team sessions)
- lib/spotter_web/components/import_modal_components.ex (add "Import Team" bulk action, team grouping UI)
- lib/spotter_web/live/pane_list_live.ex (handle bulk team import event)
- test/spotter/services/transcript_discovery_test.exs (team grouping tests)
- test/spotter_web/live/import_modal_test.exs (bulk import UI tests)

## Technical specs
- build_preview/3 must include team_name (string | nil) in the returned preview map, extracted from first JSONL line "teamName" field
- Discovery must group previews by team_name so UI can show team clusters
- Import modal must offer "Import all N team members" action when a team session is selected
- import_selected handler must iterate all team member files when bulk-importing

## Component/module usage
- TranscriptDiscovery.discover/1 — add team_name field to preview map
- TranscriptDiscovery.build_preview/3 — extract teamName from first_line_parsed
- ImportModalComponents — team grouping display, bulk action button
- PaneListLive — handle "import_team" event

## Source references
- lib/spotter/services/transcript_discovery.ex:116-147 (build_preview)
- lib/spotter_web/components/import_modal_components.ex:42-63 (transcript table)
- lib/spotter_web/live/pane_list_live.ex:270-310 (import_selected handler)

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Some team members may already be imported — skip gracefully
- Team name may be nil for non-team sessions — no grouping for those
- Large teams (10+ members) — ensure no timeout on bulk import
- JSONL files may be deleted between discovery and import — handle FileError

## Architecture constraints
- Use ash_computer for complex grouping logic
- No schema migrations
- Preserve existing single-session import flow as default

## Telemetry requirements
- Add span: spotter.import.team_bulk with attribute team_name, member_count

## Definition of Done
- [] All requirements in the task description are implemented.
- [] Tests to verify the behaviour exist or were added, and executed and pass.
- [] Relevant e2e tests were executed and pass.
- [] The changes were reviewed using code-reviewer and coderabbit:code-reviewer.
- [] After completing this task, an in-between commit was created using @handgemacht/commit-handler.
close_reason: Implemented: team_name/agent_name in previews, group_by_team, Import Team bulk action, telemetry span. 177 tests pass.

title: Render lanes through TranscriptRenderer pipeline
description:
## Why this task is needed now
Lane columns currently render raw Message data (msg.role + summarize_content) bypassing the TranscriptRenderer pipeline entirely. This means lanes show no tool blocks, no code blocks, no markdown, no styled messages — just plain text summaries. Many entries show blank content. This is the highest visual impact bug.

## Output files
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex (pipe lanes through TranscriptRenderer, use transcript_panel component)
- lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex (pass rendered_lines per lane to template)
- lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex (compute rendered_lines per lane)
- lib/spotter_web/live/transcript_computers.ex (integrate with lanes rendering)
- test/spotter_web/components/lanes_components_test.exs (rendered lane content tests)
- test/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes_test.exs (rendered_lines computation tests)

## Technical specs
- Each lane must call TranscriptRenderer.render/2 with that lane's messages to produce rendered_lines
- Lane column must use the same transcript_panel/transcript_row components as the main list view
- Lane columns must be independently scrollable
- rendered_lines must include tool_use blocks, code blocks, markdown, teammate-message styled bubbles
- Each lane panel should show the agent name as header

## Component/module usage
- TranscriptRenderer.render/2 — render messages per lane
- ParallelLanes.compute/1 — add rendered_lines to lane data
- LanesComponents.lane_column/1 — replace raw rendering with transcript_panel
- SessionLive — pass lane rendered data to template

## Source references
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:101-115 (current raw lane_column)
- lib/spotter/services/transcript_renderer.ex:1-50 (render/2 entry point)
- lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:36-44 (compute/1 lane grouping)
- lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex:491-517 (lanes vs list view render)

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Large team sessions (1000+ messages per lane) — ensure rendering doesn't block LiveView
- Empty lanes (retro-runner with few messages) — render gracefully with "No messages" placeholder
- Mixed message types (tool_use, teammate-message, system) — all must render correctly per lane

## Architecture constraints
- Reuse existing TranscriptRenderer pipeline — do NOT create a separate lane renderer
- Use ash_computer for complex lane rendering state management
- Maintain backward compatibility with non-team sessions in lanes view

## Telemetry requirements
- Add span: spotter.lanes.render_lane with attributes session_id, lane_agent_name, message_count

title: Fix timeline overlap and lane positioning
description:
## Why this task is needed now
Timeline entries in lanes view overlap visually. The time_axis component renders overlap bars that are disconnected from lane message positions. Messages use flow layout (stacked vertically) with no time-proportional positioning, causing visual confusion. Overlap bars show duplicate timestamps.

## Output files
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex (fix lane positioning — either time-proportional CSS or independent scrollable panels)
- lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex (compute time positions if using proportional layout)
- assets/css/lanes.css or equivalent (positioning styles)
- test/spotter_web/components/lanes_components_test.exs (positioning tests)
- e2e/tests/session-lanes.smoke.spec.ts (visual regression tests)

## Technical specs
- Decision needed: time-proportional positioning vs independent scrollable panels
  - Time-proportional: each message positioned based on timestamp relative to session start/end, gaps between messages visible
  - Independent panels (recommended): each lane is an independent scrollable panel, no time axis needed, simpler implementation
- If independent panels: remove time_axis component from lanes view, each lane scrolls independently
- If time-proportional: compute y-position = (msg.timestamp - session_start) / (session_end - session_start) * container_height

## Component/module usage
- LanesComponents.lane_column/1 — positioning fix
- LanesComponents.time_axis/1 — remove or fix
- ParallelLanes.compute/1 — time position calculation if needed

## Source references
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:101-115 (lane_column flow layout)
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:60-90 (time_axis component)
- lib/spotter/transcripts/parallel_lanes.ex:46-52 (timeline + overlaps computation)
- docs/design/parallel-transcript-lanes.md (design spec)

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Sessions with very short duration — ensure messages don't collapse to 0-height
- Sessions with long idle periods — avoid huge empty gaps in time-proportional mode
- Single-member "team" sessions — degrade gracefully to single panel

## Architecture constraints
- Must work with LiveView — no heavy client-side JS frameworks
- CSS-only positioning preferred over JS-computed positions
- Must be responsive for different viewport widths

## Telemetry requirements
- N/A — rendering-only change

## Definition of Done
- [] All requirements in the task description are implemented.
- [] Tests to verify the behaviour exist or were added, and executed and pass.
- [] Relevant e2e tests were executed and pass.
- [] The changes were reviewed using code-reviewer and coderabbit:code-reviewer.
- [] After completing this task, an in-between commit was created using @handgemacht/commit-handler.
close_reason: Implemented: independent scrollable panels, removed time_axis/LaneScroll, simplified SessionLive, updated CSS/tests. 1046 tests pass.

title: Add drag-and-drop reorder to lane tab bar
description:
## Why this task is needed now
The lane tab bar already exists with click-to-switch functionality, but users cannot reorder lanes by dragging tabs. Reordering should also change the visual order of lane columns. This is a UX feature requested by the user.

## Output files
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex (add phx-hook for drag-and-drop on tab bar)
- assets/js/hooks/lane_drag.js (new JS hook for SortableJS or HTML5 DnD)
- lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex (handle "reorder_lanes" event, update lane_order assign)
- assets/package.json (add sortablejs dependency if using SortableJS)
- test/spotter_web/live/session_live_lanes_test.exs (reorder event tests)

## Technical specs
- Use SortableJS (lightweight, well-maintained) via JS hook
- Hook name: LaneDrag
- On drag end: push "reorder_lanes" event with new order (list of session_ids)
- Server stores lane_order in socket assigns (not persisted to DB)
- Lane columns re-render in new order
- Tab bar reflects new order with animation
- Drag handle: the tab itself (colored dot + agent name)

## Component/module usage
- LanesComponents.lanes_panel/1 — add phx-hook="LaneDrag" to tab bar container
- SessionLive — handle "reorder_lanes" event
- LaneDrag JS hook — initialize SortableJS on mount, push events on drag end

## Source references
- lib/spotter_web/components/lanes_components.ex:30-57 (lanes_panel with tab bar)
- lib/spotter_web/live/session_live.ex:251-258 (switch_lane handler)
- e2e/support/pages/lanes.ts (lanes POM)

## Edge cases and failure handling
- Dragging to same position — no-op
- Single lane — drag disabled
- Lane removed during drag (session deleted) — handle gracefully
- Mobile/touch — SortableJS supports touch events natively

## Architecture constraints
- Must integrate with Phoenix LiveView hooks pattern
- SortableJS must be imported as ES module
- No persistence to DB — session-scoped only (socket assigns)

## Telemetry requirements
- N/A — UI-only feature

- [] Tests to verify the behaviour exist or were added, and executed and pass.
- [] Relevant e2e tests were executed and pass.

- [] After completing this task, an in-between commit was created using @handgemacht/commit-handler.
